runs.outcome: Blocked before mutation on two independent problems, and the second one challenges the instruction. Machinery: the signed-manifest relationship registry is closed to StandardNameSource PRODUCED_NAME reconciliation, revival and migration; it cannot create or delete StandardName HAS_PARENT edges, so relocating children needs a new closed reparent-and-supersede program, and raw Cypher would fail the signed receipt and replay contract. Semantics: the three live children are not the same kind of quantity. Two are flux-coordinate derivatives of the umbrella, but the third is surface_area_of_flux_surface with 20 producers, described as the total area obtained by revolving the poloidal contour through one full toroidal revolution. Reparenting that onto poloidal_plane_cross_sectional_area_of_flux_surface, which is explicitly described as excluding the swept toroidal surface, would place a swept-surface quantity under a parent that excludes swept surfaces. That is the exact distinction the locked flux-surface-area decision protects. The umbrella is therefore doing real work as a generic parent over two different area concepts, and its description says so. Recommend the umbrella survives, with the naming question being whether area_of_flux_surface is self-describing enough as a generic parent.

A reviewer or a later release cannot distinguish a minted-but-never-published roster from a real one, because the artifact carries the same shape including the pull-request number, its URL and the merge commit field. Nothing else about the predicate moves.

THIS WIDENS A GUARD, WHICH IS THE RISK. The guard exists to stop documentation being carried across a change of meaning, and documentation carried onto a name that means something else is worse than documentation regenerated. So the deliverable is not the widening alone: it is the widening PLUS the evidence that the predicate still refuses every other class. Prove, each with an explicit case, that it still returns false when the pair differs in the base, in the projection, in an operator, in a qualifier outside the locus, in the mechanism, and in the locus RELATION or TYPE even when the token also moves. WRITE THE CANONICAL ROUTE FOR CORRECTING A STANDARD-NAME FAULT, into imas_codex/core/AGENTS.md. Every fact below was measured in the last twenty-four hours; your job is to verify each against the current tree and write the route, not to rediscover them.

WHY THIS EXISTS. Correcting thirteen name spellings consumed roughly a day of coordinator and worker time across about thirty dispatched nodes, three abandoned runs, two missing-verb discoveries and two guard repairs. Total PAID pipeline spend across that day was 0.49 US dollars, for one rescore that unstuck three rows. The expensive resource was never the pipeline; it was the effort spent avoiding it. The lead's ruling: restricting pipeline spend in favour of coordinator or worker spend is a false economy, and the loop must be faster.

THE RULING THAT CHANGES, and you must reflect it. The grammar plan's migration section states "never regeneration and never a string rewrite" as the migration route. The prohibition on regeneration is WITHDRAWN. The name-generation route is free - local DeepSeek v4 flash, measured llm_cost 0.0 and paid cost 0.00 on every compose run this week - and may be used freely. The string-rewrite prohibition STANDS: a hand-written Cypher SET carries no provenance and no guarantee the result parses.

WHAT IS FREE AND WHAT IS PAID, state this plainly at the top of the route because it drives every choice below. Free: name generation and composition (local model), plus every read, census and dry run. Paid: name review, docs generation, docs review, and refine. So a name may be regenerated with abandon; a REVIEW of that name costs money, and docs are the most expensive pool.

THE ROUTE, in this order, with the reason for each step:
  1. CLASSIFY THE FAULT. A wrong spelling of an existing name is a rename. A source with no name is a generation. A wrong binding is an attachment repair. A stale scalar or a tangled lineage is an infrastructure repair. The routes differ and mixing them is what made the last cycle slow.
  2. FIX THE INFRASTRUCTURE BEFORE THE DATA. Three separate rows blocked last cycle on verb and guard coverage rather than on any naming question. A guard that refuses a legitimate class costs more than the fix: repair the guard, then apply the whole class at once.
  3. STAGE IN BULK, REVIEW ONCE. sn edit --stage-only is documented for bulk and scripted migrations - stage many, review later. Twenty-eight renames each triggering its own review cycle is twenty-eight paid reviews; staging all of them and running one batch review is one.
  4. THEN SPEND ON THE PIPELINE. Once the spellings and the infrastructure are right, run sn run and let the pools do the work they exist for. Do not hand-route what a pool claims.

THE TOOL INVENTORY, which is the half a reader most needs. For each verb state what it is FOR and the boundary that surprises people. Verify every claim against the current CLI and code before writing it:
  sn run --only, given a phase name: those phase names are NOT what they appear. compose selects generate_name AND generate_docs AND enrich_parents; review selects several pools; review_name is the exact single-pool selector. Measured twice last cycle by nodes that assumed otherwise.

COUNT ONLY LIVE BINDINGS IN THE SOURCE-MIGRATION POSTFLIGHT, AS THE PREFLIGHT ALREADY DOES.

THE MEASURED DEFECT. Six sanctioned source-backed renames are refused, once per row, with:
  RuntimeError: source migration compare-and-set changed before mutation: expected 1, moved 0
Each target is still absent and each predecessor unchanged, so every attempt rolled back with no residue. Seven sibling renames in the same cohort succeeded, which is the tell: the rows that fail are the ones whose source carries a retired binding as well as its live one.

THE MECHANISM, DIAGNOSED AND HANDED TO YOU. A repair merged earlier today added guard_comparison_bindings in imas_codex/standard_names/provenance_lifecycle.py, so the migration PREFLIGHT now counts only the bindings that could be the source's current realisation, treating a retired binding as generation provenance rather than a current one. The mutation statement's own postflight was not brought to those semantics. Inside retarget_standard_name_sources the postflight matches each expected source onto the new name and then requires:
  AND COUNT { (moved)-[:PRODUCED_NAME]->(:StandardName) } = 1
That counts EVERY binding, retired ones included. A source that legitimately retains a superseded or exhausted binding therefore holds two after a successful migration, the count returns 2, the postflight count falls below the expected cardinality, the whole statement yields no row, and the caller reports moved 0 while nothing is wrong with the migration it just performed. Confirm this reading against the code before changing it and say in your report whether you confirmed or refuted it.

Express the stage set in the Cypher from that constant rather than retyping the literals, so the two sides cannot drift apart again; if passing it as a parameter is cleaner than interpolating, do that.

Read guard_comparison_bindings first and mirror its rule deliberately: a retired binding is dropped from a comparison, a live binding always counts. The postflight and the preflight must agree on what a binding means, and this node exists because they did not.

CHECK THE WHOLE STATEMENT FOR THE SAME MISTAKE, not only the line quoted above. Any other place in that Cypher that counts or collects PRODUCED_NAME edges without excluding retired names is the same defect and belongs in this node. Report every site you found and what you did about each. If a site is correct as written because it deliberately wants all bindings, say why rather than changing it.

THE MEASURED FAILURE, AND IT IS A REGRESSION FROM AN INCOMPLETE INSTRUCTION RATHER THAN A NEW DEFECT. Six sanctioned source-backed renames are refused, once per row, with:

THE EXACT CAUSE. imas_codex/standard_names/provenance_lifecycle.py holds three places that reason about a source's PRODUCED_NAME bindings during a migration. The preflight uses guard_comparison_bindings, whose rule is: drop a binding only when its name is at a retired stage AND that name is NOT the one the caller expects. That carve-out exists because the rename transaction sets the predecessor to superseded BEFORE the comparison runs, so the expected old spelling is itself retired by the time it is compared, and a plain retired-stage exclusion would drop it.

A repair merged as 32e204607 brought the mutation precondition and the postflight to a retired-stage exclusion WITHOUT that carve-out. They now count only bindings at a non-retired stage, which drops the expected predecessor for the same reason, and the count reaches zero where one was expected. The earlier repair's own test did not catch this because the retired binding in that test was a SIBLING of the expected one rather than the expected one itself, so the carve-out was never exercised.

THE RULE ALL THREE SITES MUST SHARE. A binding is excluded from a comparison only when its name is at a retired stage AND is not named in the caller's expected set. A live binding always counts. The expected current binding always counts, whatever its stage. For the source migration the expected set is the old spelling together with the new spelling, exactly as the preflight already passes.

FIX BOTH SITES TO THAT RULE. Read guard_comparison_bindings and its preflight call site first and make the mutation precondition and the postflight agree with it rather than approximating it. WHAT MUST NOT CHANGE. A source that ends with two LIVE bindings is still a genuine cardinality fault and must still be refused. GATE AN UPSTREAM CATALOG RELEASE ON A PUBLICLY RELEASED GRAMMAR, AND STAMP THE CATALOG WITH THE GRAMMAR IT ACTUALLY USED.

THE REQUIREMENT, FROM THE LEAD. A catalog published upstream must be built against a public released standard-names grammar. It must not be a development version, must not be a release candidate, and must not be a version only this workstation can resolve. The lead also ruled that this must apply ONLY to upstream releases and must not handicap development work: a release candidate, a plain export, and a dry-run rehearsal must all remain usable exactly as they are today.

TWO DEFECTS, BOTH MEASURED. Confirm each against the code before changing it and report whether you confirmed or refuted it.

DEFECT ONE, THE STAMP IS WRONG. imas_codex/standard_names/export.py writes into the exported catalog:
    "grammar_version": imas_standard_names.__version__,
    "isn_model_version": imas_standard_names.__version__,
The standard-names package is installed editable, so that attribute carries the version baked when the editable install was built, not the grammar in the working tree. Measured on 2026-09-07 it read `0.8.1.dev32+g12b557363` from a checkout whose actual state was the v0.9.0 release. So a catalog cut today records a development grammar version that is both wrong and unreproducible. Make the stamp report the grammar the export actually used, derived from the standard-names checkout's own git identity rather than from installed distribution metadata. If both a checkout identity and a distribution version are available and they disagree, that disagreement is itself a fault worth surfacing rather than silently preferring one.

DEFECT TWO, NOTHING GATES IT. The seven export gates are graph_tests, cross_field_consistency, score_thresholds, divergence_detection, exclusion_accounting, identity_token_collision and catalog_status; none concerns the grammar. `_get_isn_dep_version` in imas_codex/standard_names/catalog_release.py looks like a check and is not one: it regex-scrapes a declared dependency string out of pyproject.toml, explicitly admits a release-candidate suffix, returns None on any exception, and feeds only a status dictionary. It reports a declaration; it never gates, and it cannot observe what was actually resolved.

WHERE THE GATE GOES. Put it in the release preflight in catalog_release.py beside the existing on-main, working-tree, synced-with-remote and CI-passed checks, and make it conditional on the release targeting the upstream remote. The release already resolves that: a final release reports `Remote: upstream` while a release candidate reports `Remote: origin`. Use that same resolved value as the discriminator so a candidate, an export and a rehearsal are untouched. Report the check in the preflight block in the same style as its neighbours, and let a dry run REPORT the verdict without blocking, exactly as the CI check already does.

WHAT THE GATE MUST ASSERT, all four, failing closed and naming which one failed:
  1. The standard-names checkout's HEAD is exactly at an annotated tag with no uncommitted modification, so the grammar has a single unambiguous identity.
  2. That tag is a final release: a plain major.minor.patch with no release-candidate, alpha, beta, development or local-version suffix.
  3. That tag is present on the upstream remote, so the grammar is public rather than local or fork-only.
  4. The matching version is published on the package index as a final release rather than a prerelease.
Assertion four needs the network. Fail closed when the index cannot be reached and say so in those words: an unreachable index is unknown, and unknown is not permission. Give it a bounded timeout so a slow index cannot hang a release.

WRITE THE FOUR AS SEPARATE FINDINGS, not one boolean. An operator who is blocked needs to know whether the fix is committing a tag, cutting a release rather than a candidate, pushing a tag public, or waiting for a publish to finish. node_definition.done_when:
DERIVE THE CATALOG'S DATA-DICTIONARY LINEAGE FROM THE SOURCES IT ACTUALLY EMITTED.

THE MEASURED DEFECT. In imas_codex/standard_names/export.py the exported catalog manifest sets
    "dd_version_lineage": ["4.0.0"],
as a hardcoded literal. Measured against the staged export of a 196-name batch on 2026-09-07, the per-source bindings in that same catalog carried version 4.1.0 on 1043 bindings and 4.1.1 on 37 bindings, and 4.0.0 on none. So the header asserts a lineage that appears nowhere in the data it describes.

THE DESIGN THE FIX MUST HONOUR, stated by the lead. A standard-name catalog is never for a single data-dictionary version. Provenance is tracked per name as each name is sourced: every source binding carries its own version sub-key, which the module's own comment already documents, and names added later will carry sources from later dictionaries. A name can be confirmed to still apply to a later version, but the binding is what records where it came from. A single catalog-wide version is therefore the wrong shape for this field regardless of which value it holds; the field is a lineage precisely because it is plural.

THE FIX. Compute the value from the distinct per-source versions actually present in the emitted entries, ordered so the result is stable across runs, so this batch reports 4.1.0 and 4.1.1 and a later batch reports whatever its sources carry. Read how the per-binding version is populated before you change anything and derive from that same value, so the header and the bindings cannot disagree. Report the exact expression you used.

THE EMPTY AND UNPINNED CASES ARE YOURS TO ESTABLISH FROM THE CODE. Establish from the code what happens when an entry has no source, or a source with no pinned version: the module already refuses a facility signal source that has no pinned version, so read that path and follow the convention it sets rather than inventing a new one. Say in your report what the field becomes for an export that emits no sourced entry at all, and why that choice is right rather than merely convenient.

DO NOT SORT VERSIONS AS STRINGS. A lexical sort orders 4.1.10 before 4.1.2 and rc9 after rc65, which has produced a wrong answer in this repository before. If the ordering matters, order by parsed numeric components; if a stable arbitrary order is sufficient, say so explicitly rather than leaving it implicit.

TESTS, in the file that already covers catalog export files; say which you chose and why.
  1. An export whose sources carry two distinct versions reports both, in the order your implementation guarantees. Prove this fails before your change against the hardcoded literal and passes after, and report both results.
  2. An export whose sources all carry one version reports exactly that one, and it is not the old literal.
  3. The empty or unsourced case behaves as you decided, asserted rather than described.
  4. A version list that would be mis-ordered by a lexical sort comes back in numeric order, so the ordering cannot regress into a string comparison.

The recorded partition: 8 rows valid with no description, which need their descriptions materialised BEFORE the validation drain can observe them, because the drain cannot observe a row it cannot audit, and the drain must then be run on exactly those ids rather than on a wider scope; 38 rows legacy quarantined, which are evidence-producing scoped audits each already carrying a per-row grammar reason, so these are REAL FINDINGS rather than damage and the correct action is to report them with their reasons rather than to clear them; and 18 rows pending, which need nothing at all because a pending row has no verdict to observe, so let them reach ordinary validation. Act only on the first subgroup, report the second with its per-row reasons, and leave the third untouched. Never clear a quarantine to make a count move: the previous pass drained 43 valid rows, observed 35, and NINE re-quarantined on genuine re-audit, five of them paid childless identities a cleanup had been refusing to touch, which established that those refusals were protecting rows whose valid status had never been observed rather than rows wrongly condemned. So a re-quarantine is a correct outcome and must be reported as one. Delete nothing: an identity carrying recorded LLM spend is undeletable by standing ruling, and the instrument for that is the LLMCost attribution rather than any provenance test. Attempt no signed manifest apply. The evidence file must carry the confirmed counts, the per-subgroup verdict, whatever was materialised and drained with its receipt, the 38 reasons, and the residue left for a later decision. Answer three specific questions with evidence. Second, whether any exit is now uncounted, which the new arithmetic refusal decides. Third, whether hot_neutral_temperature, the single identity shared with the reviewed-state population, appears published or excluded.
